items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (validateWindowName, buildWindowSpecSQL, windows field). But the dialects use single-letter lambdas (`windows.map((w) => ...)`) and import inconsistently: pg/gel use '~/sql/index.ts', mysql/sqlite/singlestore use '~/sql/functions/window.ts'.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Shared spec builder and name validation are reused, which is good. However, the same ~20-line .window() body, including the `new Proxy(this.config.fields, new SelectionProxyHandler(...))` callback resolution, is copied into all five select builders.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated at the boundary: window names (empty/whitespace), ntile/nthValue positive integers, preceding/following non-negative integers, and frame from/to ordering. Hidden tests pass 130/130 F2P, and no errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: each *SelectConfig gets an optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]`, all five dialects get the same .window() method, and the WINDOW chunk is inserted before ORDER BY only when windows exist. P2P 566/566 pass, so existing SQL is unchanged.
